preamble: In Lovono (also called Vano), a now-extinct language of Vanikoro in Temotu Province, Solomon Islands, some words with a final schwa reconstructed for Proto-Vanikoro end in -ie. Teanu, the surviving language of the island, has -o in the same words and Tanema has -a: Proto-Vanikoro *uvə 'yam' gives Teanu uo, Tanema uva and Lovono upie. The -ie reflex is not general: after k, Lovono has -a (menuka 'bird' and wauka 'louse' beside Teanu menuko and uko, the latter from Proto-Vanikoro *ukə), and the Lovono -ie forms in the dictionary follow labial consonants.

examples.note: Cognates are Teanu uo and Tanema uva 'greater yam (Dioscorea alata)'
Equivalent of Teanu iunubo 'portion of food, food parcel' and Tanema nuba; the Lovono form also shows a nasal m for the prenasalized stop
